changes: All filled fields match Wikipedia: 125 to 180 eggs a year, good sitters, 1.0 kg cock and 0.9 kg hen, single comb, white earlobes, Belgium, standard of 1930. Added egg_size small from Wikipedia's 42 to 48 g egg weight (US small grade). FAO DAD-IS (Belgium) confirms Belgian origin and egg use and describes it as a dwarf fowl related to the Brabanter, smaller and without crest. No second publisher gives weights or egg figures, so needs_review stays true.

summary.value: The Bassette Liégeoise, often just called the Bassette, is a small Belgian chicken from the Liège area of Wallonia. It counts as a true bantam because no large version exists, yet it is bigger than most bantams: cocks weigh about 2.2 pounds and hens about 2 pounds. Local people once kept these little birds to hatch partridge and pheasant eggs. From around 1917 a Brussels breeder, William Collier, selected them for a fixed type and better laying, and a standard followed in 1930. The bird has a single comb, white earlobes and slate blue beak and legs. Quail and silver quail are the usual colors. Hens lay about 125 to 180 small eggs a year and make reliable sitters and mothers. Very few birds remain, so the breed mainly interests keepers who want to preserve a rare Belgian line.
